claims: NASA primarily launches from the John F. Kennedy Space Center (KSC) on Merritt Island, Florida, particularly for major missions like Artemis II.
The John F. Kennedy Space Center (KSC) is located on the east coast of Florida near Cape Canaveral.
KSC has been the hub for American human spaceflight since 1968.
KSC utilizes launch pads such as Complex 39A and 39B.
Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida are primary NASA launch locations.
Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida are the primary site for crewed missions, Artemis lunar missions, and large payloads.
Vandenberg Space Force Base is in California.
Vandenberg Space Force Base is used for polar-orbiting satellites.
Wallops Flight Facility is in Virginia.
Wallops Flight Facility is used for small rockets and scientific missions.
SpaceX launches NASA missions from Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center.
